extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, Technology Center directors, and patent practitioners handling ex parte appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing an examiner's answer in an ex parte appeal and on when a rejection in the answer constitutes a 'new ground of rejection' (including required approvals, notification, appellant options, and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that all rejected claims are on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will presume that all of the rejected claims are on appeal except for any claims subsequently canceled by an amendment filed by appellant. Therefore, the examiner will treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal, and maintain all of the rejections set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken, unless appellant has overcome the rejection (e.g., by submitting persuasive arguments, an acceptable terminal disclaimer, or evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In situations where the appellant requests to hold a rejection in abeyance or did not present any argument on a rejection in the appeal brief, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner’s answer and should identify that the appellant has not argued the rejection in the appeal brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify how final rejection applies to amended/added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 would be entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must identify (in an advisory action) how one or more individual rejections set forth in the final rejection would be used to reject the added or amended claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many appeals contain claims not identical to those in the examiner’s final rejection (entirely new claims or amended versions), the examiner must identify in an advisory action which individual rejection(s) would be used against the added/amended claims so the applicant knows what to address on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluate positions and withdraw inappropriate rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate their position in light of the arguments presented in the brief, and should expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to in the 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS' subsection of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner withdraws all rejections of an independent claim previously under rejection while maintaining rejections of other claims, the answer should note the change of status. Include changes to dependent claim status when rejections are withdrawn. If all rejections to a dependent claim are withdrawn while the independent claim remains rejected, applicant may file an amendment under 37 CFR 41.33(b)(2) to rewrite the claim in independent form; if independent claim rejection is later affirmed on appeal, such amendment must be presented prior to expiration of the time period in 37 CFR 90.3. See MPEP §§ 1214.06 and 1214.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and required sections of the examiner’s answer (use form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prescribed form paragraphs and headings in the examiner’s answer (examples: 12.249 Examiner’s Answer Cover Sheet; 12.254 Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal; 12.255 Restatement of Rejection; 12.256 New Grounds of Rejection; 12.257 Withdrawn Rejections; 12.261 Response to Argument; 12.279 Conclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examiner notes for each form paragraph (e.g., insert mailing dates, application numbers, indicate use of paragraphs 12.255–12.257 where applicable). Use form paragraph 12.256 to introduce any new grounds of rejection and 12.257 to withdraw a ground previously made. Precede restatement (12.255) with 12.254.01 or 12.254.02 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify and prominently label new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new ground of rejection made by an examiner in an answer must be prominently identified in the 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' section under the subheading 'New Grounds of Rejection' (the examiner may use form paragraph 12.256).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must provide a concise statement of each new ground of rejection presented for review and may use form paragraph 12.279.01 to notify appellant of the reply period and to include the required approval of the TC Director or designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval requirement for new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new ground of rejection included in an examiner’s answer must be approved by a Technology Center (TC) Director or designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.39(a)(2) requires approval by the Director (delegated to TC Directors or designees). The answer must include the signature of a TC Director or designee indicating approval. If the answer contains a new interpretation/application of law, forward the answer, application file, and memorandum to the TC Director; if approved, forward to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for final approval (see MPEP § 1003).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appellant two-month reply period for new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must provide appellant a two-month time period for reply when new grounds of rejection are presented in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must within TWO MONTHS from the date of the answer either (1) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment, affidavit or other evidence, or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing each new ground of rejection. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not applicable to this TWO MONTH period; see 37 CFR 1.136(b) and 1.550(c) for other extension rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant options after new ground in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer contains a new ground, appellant must either reopen prosecution (reply under 37 CFR 1.111) or maintain the appeal (reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing each new ground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to reopen prosecution that complies with 37 CFR 41.39(b)(1) will be entered and considered and will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. A reply brief that includes any amendment, affidavit or other evidence will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 41.39(b)(1). The reply brief must address each new ground as set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newly cited evidence in answer must be designated as new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence (such as a new prior art reference, but not including a newly relied upon dictionary definition) is applied or cited for the first time in an examiner’s answer, then 37 CFR 41.39(a)(2) requires that the rejection be designated as a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citation of a new prior art reference is necessary to support a rejection, it must be included in the statement of rejection and designated as a new ground. Even if cited in minor capacity, include it and designate as new ground. See MPEP § 2144.03 for guidance on citation of a new reference supporting Official Notice taken prior to examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in the 'basic thrust' or new facts/rationales may constitute a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A position or rationale that changes the 'basic thrust of the rejection' will give rise to a new ground of rejection; reliance on the same statutory basis and prior art may nonetheless be new if it relies on new facts or rationales not previously raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite cases: In re Kronig, In re Leithem, Rambus v. Rea. However, different language or restatement that does not alter the basic thrust is not a new ground. Examiners need not use identical language so long as the basic thrust remains the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of situations that constitute a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual examples that will constitute a new ground include: changing statutory basis from 35 U.S.C. 102 to 103 (or vice versa) where issues differ; citing new calculations for overlapping ranges first identified in the answer; relying on a different structure in support of structural obviousness; pointing to different portion of the claim to maintain a 'new matter' 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from case law are provided (In re Hughes; In re Echerd; In re Kumar; In re Wiechert; In re Waymouth), illustrating that new statutory bases, new factual underpinnings, new calculations, or reliance on portions of references not previously relied upon may require designation as new ground because appellants must have a fair opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations that do not constitute a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: No new ground exists when the basic thrust of the rejection remains the same and the appellant has had a fair opportunity to react; changes in discussion/rationale, citation of different portions of the same reference that merely elaborate, changing the order of references, or relying on fewer references but the same teachings generally are not new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and case citations (In re Kronig; In re DBC; In re May; In re Cowles; In re Krammes) demonstrate that elaboration, reliance on the same teaching, or rearrangement that does not introduce new facts/rationales typically will not be a new ground. Also, when an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116/41.33 was entered for appeal with an advisory action specifying which individual rejections would apply to the amended/additional claims, rejections applied in the examiner’s answer to those amended claims are not new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground not permitted against previously allowed or objected-to claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection would not be permitted to reject a previously allowed or objected to claim even if the new ground would rely upon evidence already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such instances, rather than making a new ground in an examiner’s answer, the examiner should reopen prosecution (subject to supervisory approval) to apply the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to notify and handle examiner’s answer content when appellant did not argue a rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant did not present any argument on a rejection in the appeal brief, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner’s answer and should identify that the appellant has not argued the rejection in the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an issue raised by appellant was fully responded to under 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' no additional response is required; otherwise a full response must be provided after the designated form paragraph (12.261).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely reply to new ground(s) of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to timely respond to an examiner’s answer that included a new ground of rejection within two months, the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground may be dismissed and those claims canceled; only claims not subject to the new ground remain and the application will be forwarded to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.279.02 to notify of dismissal; insert mailing date of the examiner's answer and claim numbers of dismissed vs remaining claims. The two-month period is measured from mailing date of the examiner’s answer containing the new ground and is governed by 37 CFR 41.39(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to pay appeal forwarding fee (37 CFR 41.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid dismissal of the appeal in any application or ex parte reexamination proceeding, 37 CFR 41.45 requires payment of an appeal forwarding fee within the time permitted by 37 CFR 41.45(a), unless appellant had timely paid the fee for filing a brief required by 37 CFR 41.20(b) in effect on March 18, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate examiner notes in form paragraphs regarding the appeal forwarding fee where the notice of appeal was filed on or after January 23, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to forward examiner’s answer containing new legal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the examiner’s answer, application file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the TC Director for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved by the TC Director, the examiner’s answer should be forwarded to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for final approval. See MPEP § 1003 for procedures.
